_about: Drawn 3D board for site/boardviz (docs/how-to-contribute.md, Add a board drawing). Millimeters from the board's bottom-left corner, x right, y up, rot in degrees counterclockwise. parts: the hand-placed parts, each with a type the part library knows; a part with an id can carry a label and text shown when tapped. headers: cols x rows at 2.54 mm, pins named top row first, left column first; pins with names become tap targets. decor: two-pad parts placed by hand from the drawing, drawn but never labelled.
source: Positions read from the board overview figure in the kit's quick start guide (SWRU588), scale set from the 2.54 mm BoosterPack header pitch. Pin names from the same guide's pinout figure. Checked 2026-11-09 against a bench photo of the board (site/media/cc2340r5-blinking.jpg): antenna trace, SMA socket, LEDs, buttons and probe plug placed from it.

parts.label: The chip
parts.title: CC2340R5
parts.text: A 48 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ with 512 kB of flash and 36 kB of RAM and a 2.4 GHz radio for Bluetooth Low Energy, Zigbee and 802.15.4. Part CC2340R52E0RKP, 40-pin QFN.

parts.label: Crystal
parts.title: 48 MHz crystal
parts.text: The crystal that times the radio and the CPU. It sits just below the chip.

parts.label: Antenna
parts.title: Printed antenna
parts.text: The 2.4 GHz antenna is a trace on the circuit board itself, with no part to buy. Keep metal and hands off this end while you test range.

parts.name: Red LED
parts.label: Red LED
parts.title: Red LED on DIO14
parts.text: A user light on pin DIO14. Blinking it is the first project on this board.

parts.name: Green LED
parts.label: Green LED
parts.title: Green LED on DIO15
parts.text: The second user light, on pin DIO15.

parts.label: BTN-1
parts.title: Button 1 on DIO10
parts.text: A user button that pulls DIO10 low while you press it.

parts.label: BTN-2
parts.title: Button 2 on DIO9
parts.text: The second user button, on DIO9.

parts.label: Probe connector
parts.title: 20-pin probe connector
parts.text: The black plug on the top edge is where an XDS110 probe clips on. It carries power, SWD programming and a serial port, so the board needs no USB of its own.

parts.label: Arm 10-pin
parts.title: 10-pin debug header
parts.text: A standard Arm Cortex-M 10-pin header for an outside debug probe. It carries SWD only, so wire the serial port yourself, and power the board separately.

parts.label: BoosterPack J1, J3
parts.title: Left BoosterPack headers
parts.text: J1 is the outer column, pins 1 to 10 from the top. J3 is the inner column, pins 21 to 30. Plug-on boards stack on these.

parts.label: BoosterPack J4, J2
parts.title: Right BoosterPack headers
parts.text: J4 is the inner column, pins 40 to 31 from the top. J2 is the outer column, pins 20 to 11.

parts.label: Power pins, left
parts.title: GND, GND, 5V
parts.text: Three pins on the left edge: two grounds and the 5 V rail.

parts.label: Power pins, right
parts.title: GND, GND, 3V3
parts.text: Three pins on the right edge: two grounds and the 3.3 V rail.

parts.label: Antenna socket
parts.title: SMA antenna socket
parts.text: A gold SMA socket beside the printed antenna, for an outside antenna or a cable to test gear. The silkscreen reads Mount for CC-ANTENNA-DK.
